declarations.docstring: Associates an antitone sequence to each element of the auxiliary indexing type.
The map from auxiliary indices to antitone sequences is injective.
The auxiliary units-valued map recovers the selected unit on a diagonal element.
Below the matrix size, the auxiliary submodule has trivial intersection with the homogeneous component.
For an equivariant exact pair whose indicated weight submodules span, the associated polynomial of the middle representation is the sum of those at the ends.
The polynomial attached to the second auxiliary family is the product of all variables times the polynomial attached to the first family.
An injective equivariant linear map identifies each source weight submodule with the intersection of the target weight submodule and its range.
An equivariant linear map sends every weight submodule into the corresponding target weight submodule.
When every weight coordinate is positive, the second auxiliary family at that weight agrees with the first family at the coordinatewise predecessor.
A zero coordinate forces the indicated weight submodule of the second auxiliary family to vanish.
Membership in a weight submodule is characterized by the prescribed scalar action of every coordinate diagonal element.
A nonzero weight submodule of the base degree representation has total weight equal to the degree.
The weight submodules of the base degree representation span the whole representation.
An auxiliary natural-number-indexed family of finite-dimensional general linear group representations.
In degrees at least the matrix size, the polynomial of the first auxiliary family is a filtered finite sum of the displayed auxiliary polynomials.
An auxiliary linear map from the base degree representation to the first auxiliary representation family.
The auxiliary linear map to the first family commutes with the general linear group action.
The auxiliary linear map onto the first representation family is surjective.
An auxiliary natural-number-indexed family of subrepresentations of the displayed quotient representation.
The polynomial of the first auxiliary family admits a finite expansion by auxiliary polynomials indexed by antitone sequences that attain zero.
Below the matrix size, the first auxiliary family and the base degree representation have the same associated polynomial.
A nonzero weight submodule of the first auxiliary family has coordinate sum equal to its degree.
The weight submodules of the first auxiliary representation family span the whole representation.
Evaluating the auxiliary polynomial of an antitone sequence at one produces a natural-number value in the field.
A second auxiliary natural-number-indexed family of finite-dimensional general linear group representations.
The action on the second auxiliary family is the action on the base family multiplied by the value of the indicated units-valued map.
